Who
TASK
CODE
Handbook Chapter(s)
November General
Candidates
Start: Earliest 3rd party and independent candidates may circulate petition of qualified voter forms within the Commonwealth.
August Primary
Start: Primary candidates for November may file the certificate of candidate qualification and statement of economic interests only. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.
§ 24.2-503 and SBE Policy 2010-003
Start: Independent, political party, and 3rd party candidates for November may file ballot access documents. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.
ELECT
ELECT inquires with State, County, and City Political Party Chairs on whether a direct primary has been adopted for offices elected in November.
N/A
Party

Earliest date for political party chairs to submit adoption of primary method of nomination noticies to ELECT for office(s) elected in November.  Note: Interested local November office primary candidates may begin to pay the required primary filing fee with the the candidate's Treasurer or Director of Finance after primary adoption by the committee (§ 24.2-523).  Statewide office primary candidates pay the filing with the Department of Elections.  Once paid, the primary candidate must leave the transaction with his\her primary filing fee receipt.
Deadline for political party chairs to submit adoption of primary method of nomination noticies to ELECT for office(s) elected in November.
ELECT issues orders calling August Primary to secretary of local electoral board.
Localities
Post ELECT's order calling primary notice either on the county's/city's website, at least 10 public places, or have notice published at least once in a newpaper of general circulation.

Start (At noon): Primary candidates for U.S. Senate and local offices may file declaration of candidacy, petitions of qualified voter forms, and receipt showing payment of primary filing fee with appropriate party chairperson or with the Department of Elections no earlier than 12 pm. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

Deadline (At 5 pm): Primary candidates for U.S. Senate and local offices must file declaration of candidacy, petitions of qualified voter forms, and receipt showing payment of primary filing fee with appropriate party chairperson or with the Department of Elections no later than 5 pm. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

Deadline (At 5 pm): Primary candidates for U.S. Senate and local offices must file certificate of candidate qualification and, if necessary, the statement of economic interests. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.
Localities

Reminder: GR to confirm 1) all local candidate filings for have been submitted, reviewed, are complete and accurate, and have been processed, and 2) all candidate records in VERIS have been set up and are complete and accurate. Note: Ensuring VERIS is completely up to date satisfies the reporting requirements in § 24.2-505 & 24.2-612 (Candidate lists to ELECT).

Reminder: GR to confirm 1) all local party filings have been submitted, reviewed, are complete and accurate, and have been processed, 2) all candidate records in VERIS have been set up and are complete and accurate, and 3) unopposed candidate records are copied over to the November election in VERIS. Note: Ensuring VERIS is completely up to date satisfies the reporting requirements in § 24.2-505 & 24.2-612 (Candidate lists to ELECT).

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of candidates for U.S. Senate that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections and ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 48 hour extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify all GRs with local office elections of the deadline to file.
Parties

Deadline: Political party certification of qualified primary candidates for U.S. Senate and local offices with date, time of filing, and that a minimum number of petition signatures were found for each. If only one member of the party qualifies, they are designated as the party's nominee for November and no primary is needed for that office.
Local Electoral Board perform ballot order drawings for simultaneous primary candidate filings for local offices.
ELECT, Localities

ELECT and Electoral Boards send notice to treasurers or directors of finance to return primary filing fee(s) for unopposed, disqualified, or withdrawn primary U.S. Senate and local office candidates who withdraw before the Party Chair certifies the nominee(s).
Courts
No special election between this date and the August Primary election.
100-Day Notice: ELECT publishes the election information for use with a federal write-in absentee ballot.
Start: Political party nomination window for non-primary methods of nomination for U.S. Senate and local offices.

Start (At noon): Primary candidates for U.S. House of Representatives may file declaration of candidacy, petitions of qualified voter forms, and receipt showing payment of primary filing fee with appropriate party chairperson no earlier than 12 pm. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

Deadline (At 5 pm): Primary candidates for U.S. House of Representatives must file declaration of candidacy, petitions of qualified voter forms, and receipt showing payment of primary filing fee with appropriate party chairperson. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

Deadline (At 5 pm): Primary candidates for U.S. House of Representatives must file certificate of candidate qualification and, if necessary, the statement of economic interests. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of candidates for U.S. House of Representatives that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections an ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 48 hour extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify all GRs with local office elections of the deadline to file.

Deadline: Political party certification of qualified primary candidates for U.S. House of Representatives with date, time of filing, and that a minimum number of petition signatures were found for each. If only one member of the party qualifies, they are designated as the party's nominee and no primary is needed for that office.
SBE performs ballot order drawings for simultaneous primary candidate filings for U.S. Senate and U.S. House of Representatives
ELECT issues August Primary ballot information to General Registrars.
Start: ELECT begins reviewing ballot proofs as submitted by GRs.

ELECT sends notice to treasurers or directors of finance to return primary filing fee(s) for unopposed, disqualified, or withdrawn primary U.S. House of Representatives candidates who withdraw before the Party Chair certifies the nominee(s).
Reminder: Absentee voting equipment custodian(s) must be appointed prior to testing absentee voting equipment.
Start: Political party nomination window for non-primary methods of nomination for U.S. House of Representatives

Reminder: Testing of absentee voting equipment must be done prior to absentee voting commencement. Notice of testing date must be given to local party chairs and independent candidates. A specific date for giving notice is not set in Code. Notice must be given to primary candidates about testing in-person absentee voting equipment. The specific date is not set in Code.

Deadline (At 7 pm): For independent and political party (nominated by a non-primary method) candidates for U.S. Senate and local offices to file the certificate of candidate qualification, and, if necessary, the statement of economic interests forms. Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

Deadline (At 7 pm): For independent candidates for U.S. Senate and local offices to file the declaration of candidacy and petition of qualified voter forms with the appropriate office. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where and for an office's petition signature amount.

Deadline: Testing of absentee voting equipment must be done prior to absentee voting commencement. Reminder: ELECT will send a survey about testing absentee voting equipment. GR must respond by the deadline established in the communication.
ELECT to send absentee ballot readiness survey to GR. Reminder: Survey includes AB and L&A certification; GR's response due by deadline established in the communication.
§ 24.2-612 & DOJ Consent decree
Localities, Voters

Start: Early voting starts for August Primaries. GR must respond to ELECT's Absentee Ballot Readiness Survey.

Note for holiday: If local offices closed for Juneteenth, early voting shall start June 18th for that locality.

GR to notify disqualified local office candidates in writing via email or mail of their disqualification and the reason they failed to qualify. If candidate filing deadline is extended, this will be done after the new deadline date.

Reminder: GR to confirm 1) all local office candidate filings have been submitted, reviewed, are complete and accurate, and have been processed, and 2) all candidate records in VERIS have been set up and are complete and accurate. Note: Ensuring VERIS is completely up to date satisfies the reporting requirements in § 24.2-505 & 24.2-612 (Candidate lists to ELECT).
Deadline: Political party certification of non-primary nominees for U.S. Senate and local offices.

Disqualified 6/16 candidates (other than party nominees) may appeal their disqualification if it was due to the candidate's filed petition not containing the minimum number of signatures of qualified voters for the office sought.

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of U.S. Senate and local office candidates that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections an ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 10 day extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify all GRs with local office elections of the deadline to file.
Deadline: Election Day voting equipment custodian(s) must be appointed prior to testing election day voting equipment.
Start: First day local electoral boards can train Chief and Deputy Chief officers of election.

Reminder: New officers of election and officers starting a new term must receive training before the first election in which they will be serving as an officer of election. Note: The Code does not specify an exact number of days prior to an officer's first election date in this matter. Also, EB shall certify to ELECT all the newly trained officers. Certification to ELECT must include dates each officer completed training.
GR to give notice of date, hours, and locations for final day of voter registration.
In Person Absentee Voting must be made available for a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM for third Sunday before an election.
Deadline: Last day to apply via online, fax, or mail for an absentee ballot.
Deadline to register to vote or update an existing registration. 5:00 PM in person; 11:59 PM online
Start: Early SDR begins for August Primaries.

Reminder: Testing of Election Day voting equipment must be done prior to election day. Notice of testing date must be given to the chairman of the local committee of the political party holding the primary. A specific date for giving notice is not set in Code.
GR's office open a minimum of eight hours between 8 am - 5 pm for in-person absentee voting and absentee SDR.
In Person Absentee Voting must be made available for a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM for second Sunday before an election.

Start: If pre-processing has not already been started, on the Tuesday before an election all localities must hold the first of two mandatory pre-processing meetings to insert all absentee ballots received prior to this day into the scanning equpment.

Deadline: On the Friday or Saturday before an election all localities must hold the second of two mandatory pre-processing meetings to pre-process in order to pre-process any absentee ballots received after the initial pre-processing meeting. If you are not able to pre-process all of the absentee ballots in your possession as of the date of this meeting, then you should plan to hold a final pre-processing meeting on Monday.
Deadline: Last day to apply in person for an absentee ballot. Application must be completed at the GR office. Last day a voter can request a replacement absentee ballot. (Certain restrictions apply.)
Deadline: Last day for local electoral boards to train Chief and Deputy Chief officers of election.
Deadline: Last day a voter can request an emergency absentee ballot. (Certain restrictions apply.)

Deadline: Testing of Election Day voting equipment must be done prior to election day. Reminder: ELECT will send a survey about testing Election Day voting equipment. GR must respond by the deadline established in the communication.
ELECTION DAY
August Primary Election Day

Deadline (At 7 pm): For independent and political party (nominated by a non-primary method) candidates for U.S. House of Representatives to file the certificate of candidate qualification, and, if necessary, the statement of economic interests forms. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where.

Deadline (At 7 pm): For independent candidates for U.S. House of Representatives to file the declaration of candidacy and petition of qualified voter forms with the appropriate office. Note: Review appropriate Candidate Bulletin for who files where and for an office's petition signature amount.
Start: Local election results certification (provisional ballot meeting and canvass).

Deadline: Special election to be ordered before 90 days to be included on November ballot. If the vacancy occurs within 90 days of the next such general election and the governing body or the school board has not requested in its petition a different date for the election, the special election shall be held on the date of the second such general election.
Third Parties
Deadline: "Recognized political party" ballot recognition documents submitted to ELECT.
Deadline: Political party certification of non-primary nominees for U.S. House of Representatives.

Disqualified U.S. House of Representatives candidates (other than party nominees) may appeal their disqualification if it was due to the candidate's filed petition not containing the minimum number of signatures of qualified voters for the office sought.

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of U.S. House of Representatives candidates that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections an ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 10 day extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify all GRs with local office elections of the deadline to file.
Deadline: Losing candidate may petition for a contest.
Deadline: Special election (first November election after the vacancy) candidate filing deadline.
Deadline: Political Party Chairs must certify special election candidates nominated by non-primary methods of nomination.
November Special
Referendum\Bond Issue(s)

Deadline: A referendum election shall be ordered at least 81 days prior to the date for which the referendum election is called [§ 24.2-682(B)].  The circuit court clerk shall send copies of the writ of special election to both the local general registrar and the Department of Elections.  ELECT will enter the referendum or bond issue(s) into VERIS immediately upon receipt. The local court clerk should communicate with the GR in these instances well in advance of the deadline.  However, a phone call\email to the clerk to verify that a non-petition signature issue, i.e., governing body sourced bond issue, was issued late by the court is recommended.
Deadline: GR to notify disqualified candidates in writing via email or mail of their disqualification and the reason the candidate failed to qualify.

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of candidates that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections an ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 10 day extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify impacted GRs with local office special elections of the deadline to file.
SBE
SBE meeting to certify primary election results.

Petition for recount of local office primary deadline: Losing primary candidate must file petition with the local Circuit Court to have the local electoral board's certified result recounted.  Any calculation for the proper 10th day may only be done with the actual date of the local electoral board certification of the August Primary results. A deadline that falls on  a weekend of holiday will come forward to the next day that is not a weekend or holiday per § 1-210.

Reminder: GR to confirm 1) special election candidate and party filings have been submitted, reviewed, are complete and accurate, and have been processed, and 2) candidate records in VERIS have been set up and are complete and accurate. Note: Ensuring VERIS is completely up to date satisfies the reporting requirements in §§ 24.2-505 and 24.2-612 (Candidate lists to ELECT).
Petition for recount of August Primary offices certified by SBE Deadline: Losing candidate must file with the appropriate Circuit Court to have the SBE's certified results for such office recounted.
No special election between this date and the November general election.

Deadline: Last day for L&A before absentee voting. Absentee voting equipment custodian(s) must be appointed prior to testing absentee voting equipment. Notice must be given to local party chair and Independent Candidates about testing in-person absentee voting equipment.  The specific date is not set in Code.
Start: Absentee by mail and in-person voting begins for the November General Election.
ELECT to send absentee ballot readiness survey to GR.  Reminder: Survey includes AB and L&A certification; GR's response due by deadline established in the communication.

Reminder: New officers of election and officers starting a new term must receive training before the first election in which they will be serving as an officer of election. The Code does not specify an exact number of days prior to an officer's first election date in this matter.  Electoral Boards shall certify to ELECT all the newly trained officers.  Certification to ELECT must include dates each officer completed training.

Deadline: Last day to apply to receive an absentee ballot by mail.  Virginia Absentee Ballot Applications may be submitted online, by fax, by mail, or in-person.  Applications must be received by the General Registrar by 5 pm on 10/23/2026.
Deadline to register to vote or update and existing registration. 5:00 PM in person; 11:59 PM online
Start: Early SDR begins for November General Election.

Deadline: Last day for L&A testing. Voting equipment custodian(s) must be appointed 30 days prior to testing voting equipment. Notice must be given to local party chair and Independent Candidates about testing voting equipment.  The specific date is not set in Code.
Voters
Deadline: Last day certain voters and OOEs accepting precinct assignments after 12 pm on 11/2/26 may request an emergency absentee ballot (certain restrictions apply).
Election Day
Deadline: November absentee ballots properly returned by mail returned to GR and counted.
ELECT sends via email the final duplicate VERIS report.
ELECT likely begins reviewing abstracts of votes and certification reports.
SBE Meeting to select and approve Risk Limiting November Audits.
ELECT sends a com briefing localities on the randomly chosen congressional district, and approvals for local office RLAs.
Deadline to post Electoral Board meeting notice for conducting the November 2026 RLA.
TBD

Electoral board members needed to perform either the required or elective risk limiting audits must be available throughout the RLA period.  This would include the eleven working days between the 11/16 SBE meeting and before the State Board meeting to certify the November election on 12/7/26.  A date range of Tuesday, November 17th through Friday, December 4th is offered for planning purposes.  ELECT does not envision working on weekends or through the Thanksgiving holidays.

Petition for recount of local office Deadline: Losing candidate must file petition with the local Circuit Court to have the local electoral board's certified result recounted.  Any calculation for the proper 10th day may only be done with the actual date of the local electoral board certification of November results, e.g., the local electoral board concludes results certification on 11/10/2026 making the 10th day Friday, November 20th.
ELECT completes November Abstract review
The State Board must meet by the first Monday in December to certify the November general election results.

Contesting a November Election Deadline: A losing candidate may file his\her complaint in the appropriate Clerk's office serving notice to contest the election.  Note: Review § 24.2-806 for US House of Representatives contest provisions and § 24.2-805 for US Senate
Petition for recount of US Senate or House of Representatives Deadline: Losing candidate must file with the appropriate Circuit Court to have the SBE's certified results for such office recounted.
Deadline: Local electoral boards must conclude election results ascertainment for the August 4th Primary election and send ELECT certified copies of Abstract of Votes.
Deadline: Local electoral boards must conclude election results ascertainment for the November 3rd General election and send ELECT certified copies of Abstract of Votes.
ELECT sends com to enter all SDR VRs by COB 11/09/2026 so final duplicate VERIS report can run and be distributed on 11/10/2026.

Start: If pre-processing has not already been started, on the Tuesday before an election all localities must hold a mandatory pre-processing meeting to insert all absentee ballots received prior to this day into the scanning equipment.

Deadline: All localities must hold an additional pre-processing meeting on either Friday or Saturday immediately
preceding the election, if the total number of returned mail ballots awaiting pre-processing: 1. Is 10% or more of the total returned mail absentee ballots for the locality; and 2. Consists of at least 100 ballots.. If you are not able to pre-process all of the absentee ballots in your possession as of the date of this meeting, then you should plan to hold a final pre-processing meeting on Monday.

If the vacancy occurs within 90 days of the next such general election and the governing body or the school board has not requested in its petition a different date for the election, the special election shall be held on the date of the second such general election.
Deadline: "Recognized political party" ballot recognition documents submitted to ELECT.
Deadline: Political party certification of non-primary nominees for U.S. House of Representatives.

Disqualified U.S. House of Representatives candidates (other than party nominees) may appeal their disqualification if it was due to the candidate's filed petition not containing the minimum number of signatures of qualified voters for the office sought.

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of U.S. House of Representatives candidates that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections an ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 10 day extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify all GRs with local office elections of the deadline to file.
Deadline: Local electoral boards must conclude election results ascertainment for the August 4th Primary election and send ELECT certified copies of Abstract of Votes.
Deadline: Losing candidate may petition for a contest.
Deadline: Special election (first November election after the vacancy) candidate filing deadline.
Deadline: Political Party Chairs must certify special election candidates nominated by non-primary methods of nomination.

Deadline: A referendum election shall be ordered at least 81 days prior to the date for which the referendum election is called [§ 24.2-682(B)].  The circuit court clerk shall send copies of the writ of special election to both the local general registrar and the Department of Elections.  ELECT will enter the referendum or bond issue(s) into VERIS immediately upon receipt. The local court clerk should communicate with the GR in these instances well in advance of the deadline.  However, a phone call\email to the clerk to verify that a non-petition signature issue, i.e., governing body sourced bond issue, was issued late by the court is recommended.
Deadline: GR to notify disqualified candidates in writing via email or mail of their disqualification and the reason the candidate failed to qualify.

ELECT staff to provide ELECT Commissioner report of candidates that did not file their SBE-501 and/or SOEI by the deadline. ELECT Commissioner will present the list to the State Board of Elections an ask for a blanket extension per § 24.2-503 to determine if a 10 day extension on the filing deadline is warranted.  If SBE grants a filing extension, ELECT will notify impacted GRs with local office special elections of the deadline to file.
SBE meeting to certify primary election results.

Petition for recount of local office primary deadline: Losing primary candidate must file petition with the local Circuit Court to have the local electoral board's certified result recounted.  Any calculation for the proper 10th day may only be done with the actual date of the local electoral board certification of the August Primary results. A deadline that falls on  a weekend of holiday will come forward to the next day that is not a weekend or holiday per § 1-210.
Start: ELECT begins reviewing ballot proofs as submitted by GRs.

Reminder: GR to confirm 1) special election candidate and party filings have been submitted, reviewed, are complete and accurate, and have been processed, and 2) candidate records in VERIS have been set up and are complete and accurate. Note: Ensuring VERIS is completely up to date satisfies the reporting requirements in §§ 24.2-505 and 24.2-612 (Candidate lists to ELECT).
Petition for recount of August Primary offices certified by SBE Deadline: Losing candidate must file with the appropriate Circuit Court to have the SBE's certified results for such office recounted.
No special election between this date and the November general election.

Deadline: Last day for L&A before absentee voting. Absentee voting equipment custodian(s) must be appointed prior to testing absentee voting equipment. Notice must be given to local party chair and Independent Candidates about testing in-person absentee voting equipment.  The specific date is not set in Code.
Start: Absentee by mail and in-person voting begins for the November General Election.
ELECT to send absentee ballot readiness survey to GR.  Reminder: Survey includes AB and L&A certification; GR's response due by deadline established in the communication.

Reminder: New officers of election and officers starting a new term must receive training before the first election in which they will be serving as an officer of election. The Code does not specify an exact number of days prior to an officer's first election date in this matter.  Electoral Boards shall certify to ELECT all the newly trained officers.  Certification to ELECT must include dates each officer completed training.
Start: First day local electoral boards can train Chief and Deputy Chief officers of election.
GR to give notice of date, hours, and locations for final day of voter registration.
In Person Absentee Voting must be made available for a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM for third Sunday before an election.

Deadline: Last day to apply to receive an absentee ballot by mail.  Virginia Absentee Ballot Applications may be submitted online, by fax, by mail, or in-person.  Applications must be received by the General Registrar by 5 pm on 10/23/2026.
Deadline to register to vote or update and existing registration. 5:00 PM in person; 11:59 PM online
Start: Early SDR begins for November General Election.
GR's office open a minimum of eight hours between 8 am - 5 pm for in-person absentee voting and absentee SDR.
In Person Absentee Voting must be made available for a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 AM and 5:00 PM for second Sunday before an election.

Start: If pre-processing has not already been started, on the Tuesday before an election all localities must hold a mandatory pre-processing meeting to insert all absentee ballots received prior to this day into the scanning equipment.

Deadline: On the Friday or Saturday before an election all localities must hold the second of two mandatory pre-processing meetings to pre-process in order to pre-process any absentee ballots received after the initial pre-processing meeting. If you are not able to pre-process all of the absentee ballots in your possession as of the date of this meeting, then you should plan to hold a final pre-processing meeting on Monday.

Deadline: All localities must hold an additional pre-processing meeting on either Friday or Saturday immediately
preceding the election, if the total number of returned mail ballots awaiting pre-processing: 1. Is 10% or more of the total returned mail absentee ballots for the locality; and 2. Consists of at least 100 ballots.. If you are not able to pre-process all of the absentee ballots in your possession as of the date of this meeting, then you should plan to hold a final pre-processing meeting on Monday.
GR's office open a minimum of eight hours between 8 am - 5 pm for in-person absentee voting and absentee SDR.

Deadline: Last day for L&A testing. Voting equipment custodian(s) must be appointed 30 days prior to testing voting equipment. Notice must be given to local party chair and Independent Candidates about testing voting equipment.  The specific date is not set in Code.
Deadline: Last day certain voters and OOEs accepting precinct assignments after 12 pm on 11/2/26 may request an emergency absentee ballot (certain restrictions apply).
ELECT sends com to enter all SDR VRs by COB 11/09/2026 so final duplicate VERIS report can run and be distributed on 11/10/2026.
Deadline: November absentee ballots properly returned by mail returned to GR and counted.
ELECT sends via email the final duplicate VERIS report.
ELECT likely begins reviewing abstracts of votes and certification reports.
Deadline: Local electoral boards must conclude election results ascertainment for the November 3rd General election and send ELECT certified copies of Abstract of Votes.
SBE Meeting to select and approve Risk Limiting November Audits.
ELECT sends a com briefing localities on the randomly chosen congressional district, and approvals for local office RLAs.
Deadline to post Electoral Board meeting notice for conducting the November 2026 RLA.

Electoral board members needed to perform either the required or elective risk limiting audits must be available throughout the RLA period.  This would include the eleven working days between the 11/16 SBE meeting and before the State Board meeting to certify the November election on 12/7/26.  A date range of Tuesday, November 17th through Friday, December 4th is offered for planning purposes.  ELECT does not envision working on weekends or through the Thanksgiving holidays.

Petition for recount of local office Deadline: Losing candidate must file petition with the local Circuit Court to have the local electoral board's certified result recounted.  Any calculation for the proper 10th day may only be done with the actual date of the local electoral board certification of November results, e.g., the local electoral board concludes results certification on 11/10/2026 making the 10th day Friday, November 20th.
The State Board must meet by the first Monday in December to certify the November general election results.

Contesting a November Election Deadline: A losing candidate may file his\her complaint in the appropriate Clerk's office serving notice to contest the election.  Note: Review § 24.2-806 for US House of Representatives contest provisions and § 24.2-805 for US Senate
Petition for recount of US Senate or House of Representatives Deadline: Losing candidate must file with the appropriate Circuit Court to have the SBE's certified results for such office recounted.
